the metabolic ratio omeprazole/sulfone can be used as a probe for both CYP3A and CYP2C in one sample.
a single blood sample taken three hours after a single oral dose of omepra-zole is sufficient to assess the activities of both CYP2c19 and CYP34.

the ratio of omerprazole AUC(0–6 h)/omeprazole sulfon AUC(0 – 6 h) is an established method for phenotyping CYP3A, but the ratio of oemprazole/omepazole sulfone in one plasma sample taken 2–3 h after a dose is also a reliable method for phenotyping both CYP2c19 and CYP 3A.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of omeprazol as a probe drug for phenotyping the cytochrome P450 2C19 (CYP2C19) and CYP3As.
a novel approach for the assessment of CYP3A activity using omeprazole as a probe.
the development of a method that is suitable for routine use in a clinical laboratory for phenotyping of CYP3A activity.

omeprazole is a good substrate probe for both CYP3A and CYP2C subfamilies.

the omeprazole test is a very good probe to assess CYP2C and CYP2C9 activities, but that the omeparzole test is not a very good probe for CYP2C8 activity, CYP3A5 activity or CYP3A7 activity, and that the omeperazole test may be a very good probe of CYP3A2 activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

omeprazole 20 mg is a useful probe drug for CYP3As and CYP2Cs, and that the omeprazole metabolites omeprazole sulphone and 5-hydroxy-omeprazole are reliable markers of CYP3A and CYP2C activity, respectively.
the omeprazole test can be used as a single sample probe for both CYP3A and CYP2C, with the ratio of o/sulfone as the CYP3A probe, and the omeprazone/o ratio as the CYP2C probe.
omeprazole is a good probe for CYP2C9, CYP2C18, CYP2A6, CYP3A5, and CYP3AA, and a good probe for both CYP3A3/4 and CYP2C8, and that omeprazolesulfone is a good probe only for CYP3AA.

the use of a single plasma sample for CYP3 A4 phenotyping is possible, and that omeprazole is a good substrate for this purpose.
